structure: A short ruling file by Sam, 7 October 2026: a verbatim blockquote of five decisions (goal, DR1 backlog use, precedence, decisions/questions, themes) followed by eight numbered claims, each marked New (no earlier report question or conflict answered). Whole file read; nothing left out.

claims.statement: Wherever a real service differs from Design Release 2.1 of the GB notification service prototype, the real service changes to match Design Release 2.1.
claims.quote:
wherever the real services differ from Design Release 2.1, they
> change to match it.
claims.note: New: answers no earlier report question.

claims.statement: Which repos change (frontends, backends and others) is worked out from the evidence rather than fixed in advance.
claims.quote:
Work out from the evidence which frontends, backends
> and other repos that touches.

claims.statement: The DR1 parity backlog is not a source of requirements: nothing is built because DR1 parity says so on its own.
claims.ref: ruling-sam-2026-10-07.md claim 3; quoted paragraph on the DR1 parity backlog
claims.quote: It is not a source of requirements.
claims.note: New. The quote has an elision ([...]) before this sentence in the ruling file.

claims.statement: The DR1 parity backlog is used only where the real frontend and the prototype clash; where DR1 already judged that same difference, that judgement is followed and its row cited.
claims.ref: ruling-sam-2026-10-07.md claim 4; quoted paragraph on the DR1 parity backlog
claims.quote:
Use it only when the real
> frontend and the prototype clash: if DR1 already made a judgement on that
> difference, follow it and cite the row.

claims.statement: The prototype wins by default over what the real services do today.
claims.quote: Precedence: the prototype wins by default.

claims.statement: Only two things override the prototype: a DR1 judgement on the same difference, or a real constraint the prototype cannot express (persistence, validation, authentication, cross-service behaviour).
claims.quote:
Only a DR1 judgement or a real
> constraint the prototype can't express (persistence, validation, auth,
> cross-service behaviour) overrides it.

claims.statement: Questions for people are kept to a minimum: one is raised only when a difference is truly exceptional and neither the prototype default nor a DR1 judgement settles it.
claims.quote:
Decisions: keep questions for people to a minimum. Raise one only when a
> difference is truly exceptional and neither the default nor DR1 settles
> it.

claims.statement: Increments are grouped into themes drawn from the evidence, with boundaries set by the code each theme touches, so themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without conflicting pull requests.
claims.quote:
Themes: group the increments into themes based on the evidence. Draw the
> boundaries by the code each one touches, so themes can be built in
> parallel on separate machines without conflicting PRs.

claims.statement: The ruling does not say what counts as a difference that is 'truly exceptional', so the threshold for raising a question is left open.
claims.note: Touches claim 7. Left to the judgement of the later steps.

claims.statement: The ruling does not say how a clash is resolved where a real constraint and a DR1 judgement point opposite ways on the same difference, or where DR1 judged only part of a difference.
claims.note: Touches claims 4 and 6: both override the prototype but their ranking against each other is unstated.
